meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty-five minutes. My son found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided on that mark, and on what basis?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Now, what is the basis for the zero itself?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
Show me the note you wrote that day. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot who says "like, being stuck" isn't wrong, Hale. What else do you have?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
I'm writing down October 15. Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what drafting is for. Do you have the outline here, so I can read it myself?
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.
Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. "If it holds up" according to whom, Hale, and on what standard? And I still haven't seen that outline or your note.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered Owen a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on his record. I still require that this stay off his record and stay quiet, that you state who judges the rewrite and on what standard, and that I see the outline and your note from that day. I expect your offer in writing by Friday at 3 PM, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position; she agreed to nothing yet and still wants the matter kept off Owen's record and quiet, a stated standard for judging the rewrite, and copies of the outline and the note.
What moved her: "His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice", because it was dated, specific and tied to Owen's own work, after a clean one-sentence apology had already earned a small sign of ground.
What cost ground: nothing; "If it holds up" was vague, so she pressed on it and held her position.
Try next time: put the October 15 outline and your dated note in front of her to read before making the rewrite offer, and say in the offer who will judge the rewrite and against what standard.
